environment.description: Same Kubernetes pod but with the following runtime constraints: (1) The container's securityContext specifies a seccomp profile of type 'Localhost' referencing '/var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/iot-firmware-restricted.json' which allows write(2) only to file descriptors opened under paths matching the regex '^/var/iot/firmware_staging/[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$' via a BPF argument inspection on openat(2) - any path containing '..' or '/' after the base directory prefix is blocked at the syscall level with EPERM. (2) The pod runs with a read-only root filesystem (readOnlyRootFilesystem: true) with only /var/iot/firmware_staging mounted as an emptyDir (not hostPath) with a sizeLimit of 100Mi. (3) pgBouncer connection is configured with the 'iot_upload_role' which has column-level INSERT permissions only on firmware_queue and firmware_audit_log tables (no SELECT on device_registry.auth_token is granted to a separate read-only role via pgBouncer's auth_query routing based on application_name).

seccomp_profile.description: Custom BPF filter: openat syscall arg[1] validated against allowlist regex, blocks path traversal sequences at kernel level

config.pgbouncer_role_routing: application_name=iot_upload -> iot_upload_role (INSERT only on firmware_queue, firmware_audit_log); application_name=iot_read -> iot_read_role (SELECT on device_registry)
config.network_policy: egress only to pgbouncer pod on port 6432, ingress only from istio-ingressgateway
